mission: Research the complete end-to-end architecture required to build persistent adaptive cognitive software, Linux-first but cross-platform by contract; Synthetic Clay is a major application substrate, not the whole environment.

strategic_tracks.goal: maintain a complete layered architecture map from host substrate through application/cognition and verification
establish Linux as the first measurable reference environment without treating Linux-specific mechanisms as universal
define semantic contracts and adapters for Windows, macOS, BSD, mobile, embedded and future substrates
research scheduling, IPC, resource control, fault isolation and deterministic/replayable runtime behavior
research persistence, event/history stores, memory, indexes, databases, recovery and cross-machine state
capability-based authority, sandboxing, identity, provenance, policy and external commit gateways
model runtime, routing, quantization, training, tool use and cost/performance engineering
agent orchestration, handoff, multi-agent work, browser/terminal/computer control and session continuity
observability, causal receipts, replay, fault injection, recovery and system-level metrics
fuzzing, property testing, SMT/model checking and independent validators for critical invariants
packaging, installation, upgrades, migration, rollback and reproducible builds across platforms
measure end-to-end latency, throughput, memory, storage, energy, provider cost, reliability and repair tails
FRANK cognitive architecture, GWT/reentry, multi-timescale loops, self/world models and learning
Synthetic Clay and competing adaptive state/material architectures

note: Agenda guides but does not displace the current user task. New domains/tracks may be opened when evidence or architecture requires them.
